generated_by: hand-authored during production; every entry is added by the run that first verified the source
what_this_is: The lane-neutral registry of FIRST-HAND and OFFICIAL sources MIW has verified and intends to reuse. Oral, Written, Notes and Study production all read it. It exists so that a primary source is researched ONCE, verified, preserved, reused, and revalidated when due - rather than rediscovered from the open web on every production run.
what_this_is_not: NOT answer authority by itself. Authority derives from ISSUER + VERSION + APPLICABILITY + CURRENTNESS, never from the fact that a file or a record exists locally. A cached entry marked CURRENT_VERIFIED still gets a lightweight supersession check before it is relied on for a current/latest claim.
why_it_exists: Recorded from a real production failure. The H1 BMP MS card was authored from a currency record that was itself one edition out of date, because the original check asked 'does BMP MS supersede BMP5?' - a question that returns the launch coverage, answers correctly, and is structurally incapable of revealing that a later edition has since appeared. See query_discipline below.

query_discipline.required: What has the authoritative publisher said MOST RECENTLY about this publication or instrument?
query_discipline.rule: Both questions must be asked. The first establishes the transition; only the second establishes the present state. A correct historical transition plus a stale present state reads exactly like current truth and is the failure this registry exists to prevent.

conventions.bytes_storage: Downloadable official documents are stored beside this file under docs/sources/ and are git-ignored by extension, exactly as docs/study/sources/*.pdf already is. The DIGEST is committed here; the bytes are not, because this repository is public and the instruments are served by their own publishers.
conventions.field_vocabulary: source_id, source_class, provider, original_url, sha256, bytes and verification_status follow docs/study/historical_source_layer.json (schema miw.study.historical_source_layer.v1) so the two layers read alike.
conventions.access_discipline: Authentication, access controls, robots restrictions and publisher restrictions are never bypassed. Where bytes cannot lawfully or technically be obtained the entry is ACCESS_LIMITED and preserves metadata, the official URL, the publisher announcement and the specific verified claims - never a pretence that the document was archived.
conventions.history: A superseded entry is retained and marked, never overwritten. New official truth wins for production; the old record stays as evidence of what was true when.

currentness_states.CURRENT_VERIFIED: Verified against the issuer's own most recent statement at checked_on.
currentness_states.CURRENT_BUT_RECHECK_ON_EVENT: Believed current, but a named event could change it before any date-based review would.
currentness_states.HISTORICAL_SUPERSEDED: A later version exists. Retained as predecessor evidence; must not be used as current truth.
currentness_states.FUTURE_ADOPTED_NOT_EFFECTIVE: Adopted with a known effective date still ahead; does not govern sittings before it.
currentness_states.ACCESS_LIMITED: Identity and issuer verified, but the document's own bytes could not lawfully or technically be retrieved. Claims are limited to what the publisher has stated publicly.
currentness_states.CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED: Not established. Barred from candidate-facing use.

sources.edition: The resolution as adopted 23 May 2024, held in full; plus IMO's January 2026 publication supplement to the 1991 Edition (sales number I240E), which carries the same amendment INCOMPLETELY
sources.issuing_authority: International Maritime Organization
sources.issuing_authority_note: IMO itself, as publisher of the Code and of its own supplement. Tier 1 - this is not a class-society or P&I restatement.
sources.source_type: official publication supplement carrying an adopted MSC resolution
sources.authority_rank: Mandatory. The Grain Code is given force by SOLAS chapter VI, part C, regulation 9; MSC.552(108) amends the Code itself.
sources.access_note: TWO IMO FILES ARE HELD AND THEY DO NOT AGREE. The AUTHORITY is the resolution itself (6 pages, full text layer, operative clauses and complete annex), retrieved from IMO's resolutions index. The companion is IMO's January 2026 publication supplement (132,651 bytes, sha256 2201d471db0ebac7f8c4f23ad82c0a6f6e141c57810d37190e513a10b1fe1432), which is INCOMPLETE in two ways: it OMITS annex item 6 (the A 12.3.3 cross-reference repair) and carries NO operative clauses at all. This registry entry originally cited the supplement alone; the resolution was obtained after an independent reviewer challenged the amendment list, and the discrepancy is the reason the entry now names the resolution as authority. A supplement to a sales publication is an editorial aid, not the instrument. Both files are filed in the shared desktop-team corpus at 03-imo-instruments/Grain-Code/ with the discrepancy recorded in its INSTRUMENT_LOG.md.
sources.publication_date_note: Supplement dated January 2026; the resolution it carries was adopted 23 May 2024.
sources.effective_date_note: MSC.552(108) entered into force 1 January 2026 and applies to both new and existing ships - there is no newbuilding-only limb.
sources.supersedes_note: Amends the 1991 Edition; it does not replace the Code.
sources.checked_how: Asked the publisher-anchored question rather than the supersession question: what is the most recent Grain Code amendment IMO itself publishes? IMO's current supplement to the 1991 Edition is the January 2026 one and its whole content is MSC.552(108). Independently re-checked against MSC 109, MSC 110 and MSC 111 outcomes - MSC 111 (13-22 May 2026) adopted the MASS Code, SOLAS IV/V amendments, the ESP Code and IMDG 43-26, and no Grain Code amendment.
sources.revalidation_note: Not yet confirmed against the official IMO depositary/status list, which is the stronger check this corpus uses elsewhere. Logged as RQ-G02 in the shared corpus review queue. RQ-G01 update 2026-09-04: the base instrument was acquired (SRC-GRAINCODE-MSC23-59). The depositary/status-list check flagged as RQ-G02 is still outstanding and is unaffected by that acquisition.
verified_claims: Adopted by MSC at its 108th session by resolution MSC.552(108) on 23 May 2024, under SOLAS article VIII(b)(iv); deemed accepted 1 July 2025 under article VIII(b)(vi)(2)(bb); in force 1 January 2026 under article VIII(b)(vii)(2).
The resolution contains NO application clause, so it binds new and existing ships alike. This can only be established from the resolution - the supplement carries no operative clauses.
The Grain Code was adopted by resolution MSC.23(59) and is mandatory under SOLAS chapter VI; the amendment procedure is article VIII(b) read with regulation VI/8.1.

New definition A 2.8: "specially suitable compartment, partly filled in way of the hatch opening, with ends untrimmed" - not filled to the maximum extent in way of the hatch opening but filled to a level equal with or above the bottom edge of the hatch end beams, and not trimmed outside the periphery of the hatch opening by A 10.4.
New A 10.4 permits the grain outside the hatch periphery to lie at its natural angle of repose and allows dispensation from trimming the ends.
A 10.7 (ex 10.6) replaced: only the free surface in way of the hatch opening need be level in such a compartment.

New B 1.1.5: surface assumed to slope in all directions at 30 degrees from the lower edge of the hatch end beam; if feeding holes per table B 1-2 are provided and the free surface in way of the hatch opening is above them, from the mean line on the hatch end beam as shown in figure B-1.
B 1.5 replaced: total heeling moment = 1.12 x calculated transverse heeling moment, now covering the new category as well as partly filled compartments.
New Part B section 4: B 2 provisions for filled-and-trimmed compartments apply, except that after shifting the surfaces are assumed at 25 degrees to the horizontal.

Sixteen numbered annex items in total. Consequential cross-reference and renumbering changes in A 10.3.1, A 10.10.3, A 12.3.3 (annex item 6, under heading 12 Divisions loaded on both sides - PRESENT IN THE RESOLUTION AND ABSENT FROM THE SUPPLEMENT), A 14.1, B 1.2, B 2.6, B 2.8, B 2.9, B 3.1 and renumbered B 5.
claims_NOT_established: That MSC.552(108) requires the approved grain loading manual or Document of Authorization to be updated. This is widely and correctly stated as PRACTICAL GUIDANCE by class societies and P&I clubs (LR class news 09/25, Britannia, BIMCO, NorthStandard) and follows from the ship only being loadable to a condition its approved booklet covers - but it is NOT in the amendment text and must not be attributed to the resolution.

Anything about the Grain Code outside this amendment delta. NOTE, UPDATED 2026-09-04: the second half of the original wording here said the 1991 base publication is NOT held (RQ-G01). That is no longer true in substance - the Code as ADOPTED is now held as the annex to MSC.23(59) and registered as SRC-GRAINCODE-MSC23-59 - but this row still establishes nothing beyond its own amendment delta, and the base row is an adopted baseline rather than a consolidated edition. RQ-G01 is closed in substance and remains open in form.

s.4(2)(a): six members of Parliament - four elected from amongst themselves by members of the House of the People, two by members of the Council of States.

s.4(2)(b): not exceeding sixteen other members, at least four of whom shall be women, representing the Central Government, ship owners, seafarers and such other interests as the Central Government considers ought to be represented, with a proviso requiring an equal number of ship owner and seafarer representatives. Statutory maximum therefore 22.
s.4(4): the Central Government nominates one of the members as Chairperson.
s.4(5): such a member or Chairperson does not hold an office of profit for article 102(1)(a).
s.4(6): the Board ADVISES the Central Government on matters relating to Indian shipping including its development, and on other matters referred to it under the Act.
s.4(7): the Board may regulate its own procedure.
s.4(8)/(9): term, casual vacancies, allowances, the Chairperson's service conditions and the Board's staff are as prescribed - the hook for the 2026 Rules.
s.5 constitutes a separate Seafarer's Welfare Board.
Part V (Seafarers) applies from s.54. s.63 carries the marginal note 'Agreement with seafarers'.

s.63(1): the master or owner of every Indian vessel, or the recruitment and placement service agency for an Indian or foreign vessel, shall enter into a seafarers' employment agreement in such form and manner as may be prescribed with every seafarer engaged, and shall submit a copy thereof to the shipping master.

s.63(2): saving for the master, owner or agent of an Indian vessel registered at a port outside India who has an agreement made in due form according to the law of that port or of the port of engagement, permitting engagement in any Indian port of CDC-holding seafarers under (a) and (b).

s.63(3): a seafarer shall, before signing a seafarers' employment agreement, be given an opportunity to examine and seek advice on the agreement to ensure that he has freely entered into it with sufficient understanding of his rights and responsibilities.

s.64(1): every ship owner of an Indian vessel shall ensure that full payments due to seafarers are made at not later than monthly intervals and that they are given a monthly account of payments due and amounts paid, including wages and additional payments. s.64(2): unpaid wages continue at the last rate payable under the agreement until paid, with interest as prescribed, subject to three exceptions (reasonable mistake, reasonable dispute as to liability, and the further ground stated in the sub-section).

s.78(1): the Central Government may, to give effect to Part A of the Code of the Maritime Labour Convention, make rules on the listed matters, which include (e) seafarers' employment agreements and (f) payment of wages.

s.83(1): where under the agreement with the seafarer any dispute arises between the master, ship owner or his agent and any of the seafarers of the vessel, it shall be submitted to the shipping master.

s.91, Explanation, clause (c): 'shipping master' is defined by reference to the port at which the seafarer entered into, or is believed to have entered into, an agreement, or where he did not enter into one in India, the port to which he has returned or is expected to return. LOCATOR CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (CORR-MSACT2B-GREEN-20260904): this claim was registered against 's.93(c)' on 2026-09-02. The PROPOSITION is correct and is unchanged; only the LOCATOR was wrong. s.93 is 'Inspection by shipping master, etc.', has clauses (a) and (b) with sub-clauses (i)-(iv) and an Explanation defining 'international voyage', and has no clause (c). The definition sits in the Explanation to s.91 ('For the purposes of this section'), clause (c). Re-read from the held PDF text layer, sha256 6fb38616ed8b82ae7e831e5589ffd59a7b27e13d55b1728940fe25892f758f63.
s.94(1): a seafarer is deemed a serving seafarer during the period commencing on the date of the agreement with seafarers and ending thirty days after final discharge from that agreement.

SECTION MAPPING PASS, 2026-09-04 (GPT REVIEW PASS 2B). Each section below was read directly from the held PDF's text layer and occurs exactly once as an operative section. TWO EXTRACTION HAZARDS RECORDED FOR ANY FUTURE READER: (1) the Act's PDF separates a section number from its text with a 0x03 control byte as well as with a space, so a naive '^[0-9]+[.]\\s' scan silently under-reports - s.319 was missed exactly this way on the first attempt; (2) the s.281(2) penalty table renumbers its rows 1..N, so table rows must be excluded before a section number is resolved.

Part structure: I ss.1-3; II ss.4-13; III ss.14-44 (Registration of Vessels); IV ss.45-53 (Maritime Education and Training); V ss.54-113 (Seafarers); VI ss.114-130 (Safety and Security); VII ss.131-143 (Prevention and Containment of Pollution from Vessel and Response); VIII ss.144-152 (Survey, Audit and Certification); IX ss.153-222 (Maritime Liability and Compensation); X ss.223-230 (Marine Incident and Emergency Response); XI ss.231-232 (Investigation and Inquiries on Marine Casualties); XII ss.233-260 (Wreck and Salvage); XIII ss.261-280; XIV ss.281-292 (Penalties and Procedures); XV ss.293-324 (Miscellaneous); XVI s.325.

s.12(1): the Central Government may establish a shipping office at every port it thinks necessary and appoint thereto (a) a shipping master and as many deputy and assistant shipping masters as required, (b) a director and deputy/assistant directors, and (c) seafarer's welfare officers.

s.15(1): no vessel shall be an Indian vessel unless owned by (a) a citizen of India including a Non-Resident Indian or an Overseas Citizen of India, (b) a company or body established by or under a Central or State Act having its registered office or principal place of business in India, or (c) such other person or body as the Central Government may notify - in such proportion of ownership as may be notified. The Act's term of art is 'Indian vessel', not 'Indian ship'.

s.18: the principal officer of the Mercantile Marine Department, or such person as the Central Government may by notification authorise, shall be the Registrar of Indian vessels at the specified port of registry.
s.20(9): every Registrar shall keep a register book, make entries in that book and maintain the records of vessels registered under the provisions of the Act, in such manner as may be prescribed.

s.46(1): an officer notified by the Central Government as the issuing authority shall, subject to the STCW Convention, grant a certificate of competency or certificate of proficiency for different grades of seafarers with such requirements and procedures as may be prescribed.

s.48(6): if it appears to the issuing authority that a holder obtained the certificate on false or erroneous information, or is guilty of indiscipline or misconduct, incompetency, or any act of omission or commission or compromise to safety, security or prevention of pollution, it may, after due investigation, by order withdraw, suspend or cancel the certificate; the proviso requires a reasonable opportunity of being heard. s.48(7): the holder may appeal against that order before the officer the Central Government notifies as appellate authority.

s.62: seafarers may be engaged only by a recruitment and placement service agency licensed under Part V, or by the owner of an Indian vessel for a vessel owned by him. s.62(2) bars carrying on recruitment and placement business without a valid licence, engaging a seafarer without a continuous discharge certificate and seafarer's identity documents, and demanding or receiving any fee or charge from a seafarer for recruitment, placement, onboard training or employment, with a proviso allowing medical/CDC/passport costs to be borne by the seafarer but requiring visa costs to be borne by the ship owner.

s.83: a dispute under the agreement with the seafarer is submitted to the shipping master, who must hear the parties and pass a reasoned award in writing within thirty days (extendable once by a further thirty for sufficient cause), which is conclusive as to the rights of the parties; the award is enforceable under the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 as if it were a decree of court; the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 does not apply.

s.131: Part VII applies to (a) Indian vessels and every other vessel registered in India, (b) vessels other than Indian vessels, (c) vessels not entitled to fly the flag of India but operating under India's authority, (d) vessels entering an Indian port, shipyard, offshore terminal or place or the coastal waters, (e) any incident of marine casualty or act relating to such casualty occurring with grave and imminent danger to the Indian coastline, coastal waters or related interests, including incidents on the high seas, and (f) ports for the purpose of providing reception facilities.
s.133(1): save as otherwise provided, all vessels shall be under an obligation to prevent discharge or emission of harmful substances or mixtures containing harmful substances.

s.138(1): where an incident in which cargo or harmful substances escape or are likely to escape causes or threatens to cause pollution, the master shall report the particulars to the prescribed authority in the prescribed manner. s.138(2): on receiving that information the Central Government may direct the owner, agent, master, charterer, operator, lessee or licensee, by notice served on him, to prevent escape, remove the cargo or substances, remove the vessel, and remove slicks on the surface of the sea.

s.224(a): 'marine incident' means an event, or sequence of events, occurring directly in connection with the operation of a vessel that endangers, or if not corrected would endanger, the safety of the vessel, its occupants or any other person or the environment, and INCLUDES marine violation, marine casualty, marine disaster, cyclones, storms or other adverse weather events, very serious marine casualty, and such other events as the Central Government may notify. IMPORTANT BOUNDARY: the phrase 'very serious marine casualty' occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the whole Act, inside this inclusion list. The Act NAMES the term; it does NOT define it. The definition remains Casualty Investigation Code (MSC.255(84)) terminology, and no candidate-facing card may say the Act defines it.

s.231(1)(a)-(g): for the purposes of investigation and inquiries under Part XI, a marine casualty is deemed to be an event or sequence of events resulting in any of seven limbs - (a) a vessel lost, abandoned, stranded or materially damaged on or near the coast of India; (b) a vessel causing loss or material damage to another vessel or to external infrastructure; (c) loss of life or presumed loss of life; (d) such loss, abandonment, stranding, material damage or casualty to an Indian vessel anywhere with a competent witness found in India; (e) an Indian vessel lost or supposed lost with evidence obtainable in India; (f) pollution or severe environmental damage, actual or potential, within the coastal waters; and (g) fire or explosion on an Indian vessel anywhere, or on another vessel on or near the coast of India.

s.231(2): notice of the marine casualty must be given WITHIN TWENTY-FOUR HOURS of the occurrence, by the ship owner, manager, operator, company, pilot, harbour master, master or other person in charge of the vessel (or of each vessel where two are concerned), to the officer appointed in this behalf by the Central Government.

s.231(3)-(4): on receiving that notice the officer shall forthwith inform the Central Government in writing and proceed to make a PRELIMINARY INQUIRY into the marine casualty, and shall on completion furnish his report to the Central Government or the authority it appoints.

s.231(5)-(6): the Central Government may, for the purposes of the investigation, appoint a body to conduct a MARINE SAFETY INVESTIGATION in accordance with the Safety Convention; that body shall make a preliminary assessment of the marine casualty, conduct the investigation to ascertain its causes and circumstances, and submit its report to the Central Government.

s.232: on receipt of the marine safety investigation report under s.231(6), or if the Central Government is of the opinion that prima facie there exists incompetency, misconduct or violation of any law in force on the part of any person, it may (a) initiate administrative action and (b) direct the officer or authority having jurisdiction over the area to initiate proceedings against that person in accordance with such law.

IMPORTANT NEGATIVE, established by whole-document search of the held PDF: the expression 'formal investigation' occurs ZERO times in the Merchant Shipping Act 2025. The 1958 framework's preliminary-inquiry / formal-investigation pairing is NOT carried forward under that name. Part XI is a RESTRUCTURE, not a renumbering, and no candidate-facing card may present 'formal investigation' as 2025 Act machinery.

IMPORTANT NEGATIVES for pollution response, established by whole-document search: 'contingency plan' ZERO occurrences, 'OPRC' ZERO, 'NOS-DCP' ZERO, 'national oil spill' ZERO. The National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan is therefore NOT named or created by the Act; it is a separate national administrative plan and must be presented as such.

IMPORTANT NEGATIVE for chief-engineer handover, established by whole-document search: 'handover', 'hand over', 'taking over', 'taking-over', 'delivery of charge' and 'chief engineer' each occur ZERO times in the Act. There is NO CE takeover or handover provision in the Merchant Shipping Act 2025, and none may be asserted.

s.281(1): residual penalty - any person who contravenes any provision of the Act or any rule or notification, or fails to comply with any provision it was his duty to comply with, is liable to penalty or guilty of an offence, and where no penalty or punishment is specially provided is liable to penalty which may extend to fifty thousand rupees. s.281(2): the contraventions in column (2) of the table are liable to the extent of penalty in column (4).

s.282(1): the authority for imposing the penalty under s.281(2) is the PRINCIPAL OFFICER. s.282(2)-(3): a person aggrieved may appeal to the Director-General within thirty days, and the appeal is disposed of within thirty days. s.282(4): no order without a reasonable opportunity of being heard. s.282(5): a first contravention may be compounded by a designated officer. s.282(6): an undeposited penalty is recoverable as an arrear of land revenue.

s.287(1): where the person committing an offence under the Act is a company, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and responsible to, the company for the conduct of its business, as well as the company itself, is deemed guilty and liable to be proceeded against and punished, subject to the due-diligence proviso.

s.290(1): where under the Act a vessel is authorised or ordered to be detained, any commissioned officer of the Indian Navy or Indian Coast Guard, or other person specified, may detain it. s.290(3) is the sub-section whose contravention - taking to sea a person authorised to detain or survey the vessel - is penalised through the s.281(2) table.

s.301: the Director-General may, if satisfied in the public interest or in the interest of Indian shipping that it is necessary, give BY NOTICE, CIRCULAR, ORDER OR GUIDELINES in writing such directions as he thinks fit to any vessel, seafarer, tindal, ship owner or his agent, maritime training institute, recruitment placement service provider, port, or person or body of persons.

s.312: the CENTRAL GOVERNMENT may, by order, cancel or suspend any certificate granted under the Act to any seafarer for a specified period where (a) an inquiry report or investigation report reveals incompetency or misconduct, (b) in a case of collision the seafarer failed to render assistance, (c) the seafarer has been convicted of an offence under the Act or has committed a non-bailable offence under any other law in or outside India, (d) a casualty was caused by the seafarer's wrongful act or default, or (e) the seafarer contravenes the Act; the proviso requires an opportunity of being heard. This power is DISTINCT from, and additional to, the issuing authority's power under s.48(6), and the two must not be merged.
s.319(1): without prejudice to any other power to make rules contained elsewhere in the Act, the Central Government may make rules generally to carry out the provisions of the Act.

s.320(1): all rules made under the Act shall be published in the Official Gazette. s.320(2): a rule may direct that a breach is liable to penalty up to fifty thousand rupees, with a continuing-breach penalty up to five thousand rupees for every day after the first. s.320(3): every rule shall be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days, subject to modification or annulment, without prejudice to anything previously done under the rule.

The saving is therefore Part XIV MINUS section 411A - s.411A is itself repealed, and any card stating the saving must carry that limb. s.324(2): notwithstanding the repeal, (a) rules, regulations, bye-laws, orders, notifications and exemptions continue as if made under this Act until revoked; (b) offices, officers and bodies continue; (c) a document referring to a repealed enactment is construed as referring to this Act; (d) fines remain recoverable; (e) offences may still be prosecuted and punished; and (f) vessels registered under the repealed enactments continue.

verified_claims: The framework is built on eight pillars: Green Shipbuilding and Retrofits; Green Ports; Green Ship Recycling; Green Finance; Green Skill; Alternate Fuels; Green Technology; Pollution Prevention / Waste Management.

Maritime INDIA @ Net Zero is described as a multi-ministerial platform to translate the National Green Shipping Policy into coordinated national action; a workshop was held on 14-15 January 2026 at the India Habitat Centre with 312 participants.

Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines were issued by MoPSW in 2023 and require, among other things, all major ports to achieve 60% renewable electricity consumption by 2030, shore power connectivity at major ports on specified timelines, ISO 14001 certification, and greenhouse-gas inventories with carbon emissions tracked per tonne of cargo handled.

India's port decarbonisation is guided by Harit Sagar carbon accounting rather than by a port equivalent of the MARPOL Annex VI CII, which applies to ships of 5,000 GT and above.

The Green Tug Transition Programme was LAUNCHED IN OCTOBER 2024 and is described as India's most advanced vessel-level decarbonisation initiative. Cochin (KPL) is planning green tug procurement only after its current diesel tug contract expires in August 2027 - it is NOT a Phase 1 port. India's first all-electric tug, built by Atreya Shipyard for Deendayal with Kongsberg permanent-magnet propulsion, was expected by late 2026. About 100 green tugs are in the procurement pipeline at approximately Rs 12,000 crore.

Renewable energy was 15.48% of total electricity consumption across Indian major ports as of 2023-24; Deendayal Port Authority is at 69.41% and Mumbai Port Authority at 87.22%, both already past the 60% target, and nine major ports are on track for 2030.

Harit Sagar requires an annual port-level GHG inventory and reduction targets "aligned with the IMO Port Carbon Intensity Indicator (PCII) framework"; a Port CII concept therefore EXISTS, while Indian port performance is measured as carbon per tonne of cargo handled against Environmental Performance Indicators.

Annex item 26 replaces paragraph 18.4.1.1.1. The replacement requires the master of the receiving ship or their representative and the representative of the bunkering source (the Persons In Charge) to agree in writing, before any bunkering operation commences, the transfer procedure including cooling down and if necessary gassing up; the maximum transfer rate at all stages; minimum and maximum limiting transfer pressure and temperature; bunkering line PRVs settings; and volume to be transferred.

Annex item 11 replaces paragraph 8.4.1: the bunkering manifold shall be designed to withstand the external loads during bunkering, and the connections at the bunkering station shall be arranged to achieve a dry-disconnect operation in one of three ways - a dry-disconnect / connect coupling in accordance with a standard at least equivalent to those acceptable to the Organization; a manual connect coupler or hydraulic connect coupler used to connect the bunker system to the receiving vessel bunkering manifold presentation flange; or a bolted flange-to-flange assembly.

Annex item 12 adds new paragraphs 8.4.2 and 8.4.3. 8.4.2 requires the second and third connection arrangements to be combined with operating procedures that ensure a dry-disconnect is achieved, subject to special consideration informed by a bunkering-arrangement risk assessment conducted at the design stage, with the fuel handling manual required by 18.2.3 documenting that the assessment was conducted and that special consideration was granted. 8.4.3 requires an emergency release coupler (ERC) / Emergency Release System (ERS) or equivalent means, unless installed on the bunkering supply side of the bunkering line, enabling a quick physical disconnection dry break-away of the bunker system in an emergency event.
New paragraph 2.2.43 defines 'ship constructed on or after 1 January 2026'.
The resolution does NOT amend the annex to part C-1 - the LNG Bunker Delivery Note. The only occurrence of 'Part C-1' in the document is the part heading that introduces the chapter 18 amendment.

sources.title: Resolution MEPC.412(84) - Amendments to the 2022 Guidelines on operational carbon intensity indicators and the calculation methods (CII Guidelines, G1)
sources.edition: The resolution as adopted 1 May 2026, held in full (4 pages, MEPC 84/16/Add.2 annex 14)
sources.issuing_authority: International Maritime Organization

sources.supersedes_note: Amends resolution MEPC.352(78); it does not replace the G1 Guidelines.
sources.checked_how: The publisher-anchored question was asked, not the supersession question. IMO's own Index of MEPC Resolutions and Guidelines related to MARPOL Annex VI was opened and its whole G1 lineage read: MEPC.336(76), revoked by MEPC.352(78); MEPC.352(78), the 2022 Guidelines; MEPC.412(84), amending MEPC.352(78). MEPC.412(84) is the LAST G1 item on the issuer's own index. Independently: MEPC 85 sits 30 November - 3 December 2026, so as at 5 September 2026 no session has met since MEPC 84 that could have moved it.
sources.revalidation_note: Due at MEPC 85 (30 Nov - 3 Dec 2026). Phase 2 of the short-term measure review is expressly revising CII metrics, so this row is expected to move rather than merely to be reconfirmed.
verified_claims: Adopted on 1 May 2026 at MEPC 84; published as annex 14 to MEPC 84/16/Add.2.
It REPLACES section 4.2 of the 2022 CII Guidelines (G1) in its entirety.
Supply-based transport work Ws = C x Dt remains the proxy for the attained annual operational CII of individual ships.

C is the ship's CAPACITY and is SHIP-TYPE SPECIFIC. Deadweight tonnage (DWT) is used for bulk carriers, tankers, container ships, gas carriers, LNG carriers, general cargo ships, refrigerated cargo carrier and combination carriers.
Gross tonnage (GT) is used for cruise passenger ships, ro-ro cargo ships (vehicle carriers), ro-ro cargo ships and ro-ro passenger ships.
Dt is the total distance travelled in nautical miles in a given calendar year, BOTH under way and not under way, as reported under the IMO DCS.

Footnote 1 defines DWT as the difference in tonnes between the displacement of a ship in water of relative density 1,025 kg/m3 at the summer load draught and the ship's lightweight; footnote 2 refers GT to the 1969 Tonnage Convention.

A note records that data on actual transport work reported under the enhanced granularity of the IMO DCS may be considered FOR ANALYTICAL PURPOSES during phase 2 of the review - it is not the calculation basis.
claims_NOT_established: Anything about the G1 Guidelines outside this amendment delta. Section 4.2 is the only section MEPC.412(84) touches; the rating bands, reference lines and reduction factors are G4/G2/G3 and are separate instruments.
Any entry-into-force or application date for the amendment. The resolution states none and none may be attributed to it.

verified_claims: The title of UR Z18 is 'Survey of Machinery'. Section 1.3 is Continuous Surveys, 1.5 Planned Maintenance Scheme (referring to UR Z20), 1.6 Condition Monitoring / Condition Based Maintenance (referring to UR Z27).
1.3: special surveys of machinery may be carried out on a continuous survey basis, in which case the interval between consecutive examinations of each item is not to exceed five (5) years.

Section 2 'Survey of Steam Boilers' is a STRUCTURALLY SEPARATE section with its own clock. 2.1: water tube boilers used for main propulsion including reheat boilers, all other boilers of essential service, and boilers of non-essential service with working pressure exceeding 0.35 N/mm2 and heating surface exceeding 4.5 m2 are to be surveyed internally, a minimum of two internal examinations during each 5-year special survey period, and the interval between any two such examinations is not to exceed 36 months; an extension of up to 3 months may be granted in exceptional circumstances.

2.2: external survey of boilers including test of safety and protective devices, and test of the safety valve using its relieving gear, is to be carried out annually within the Annual Survey window. verified_claims: Z20 (May 2001), Rev.1 July 2018, Rev.2 May 2019; Rev.2 changes uniformly applied to surveys commenced on or after 1 July 2020.

1.1.1-1.1.4: PMS is an ALTERNATIVE to Continuous Machinery Survey; surveys are considered on the basis of intervals between overhauls recommended by manufacturers, documented operator's experience and a condition monitoring system where fitted; the scheme is LIMITED to components and systems covered by CMS; items not covered by PMS are surveyed and credited in the usual way.

1.2.1: in general PMS intervals shall not exceed those specified for CMS, but for components maintained on running hours longer intervals may be accepted if based on the manufacturer's recommendations.

1.3.1: 'The chief engineer shall be the responsible person on board in charge of the PMS.' 1.3.2: overhaul documentation shall be reported and signed by the chief engineer. 1.3.3: access to computerized systems for updating the maintenance documentation and programme shall only be permitted by the chief engineer or other authorized person.

2.1.1-2.1.3: the PMS shall be programmed and maintained by a computerized system (not applied to already-approved schemes); approved per each Member Society's procedure; computerized systems shall include back-up devices updated at regular intervals.

2.2.1 lists SIX documents for approval: organization chart identifying areas of responsibility; documentation filling procedures (so printed in the UR); listing of equipment to be considered by classification in PMS; machinery identification procedure; preventive maintenance sheet(s) for each machine; listing and schedule of preventive maintenance procedures.

2.2.2 lists FOUR categories to be available on board: all clauses in 2.2.1 up to date; maintenance instructions (manufacturer's and shipyard's); reference documentation such as trend investigation procedures; records of maintenance including repairs and renewals carried out.

2.3.1: on approval a 'Certificate of Approval for Planned Maintenance Scheme' is issued; HOWEVER other equivalent certification or class notation may be issued according to the procedure in use in each individual Member Society; in any case the certification is to be kept on board.

2.3.2 an implementation Survey confirms the validity of the certificate/class notation. 2.3.3 an annual report covering the year's service is reviewed by the Society. 2.3.4 an Annual Audit maintains the validity of the PMS.

2.3.5: the survey arrangement can be CANCELLED by the Society if PMS is not being satisfactorily carried out, judged from the maintenance records or the general condition of the machinery, or when the agreed intervals between overhauls are exceeded. 2.3.6 sale, change of management or transfer of class causes the approval to be reconsidered. 2.3.7 the shipowner may cancel at any time in writing, items inspected since the last annual survey credited at the attending surveyor's discretion.

3.1.1: the Implementation Survey shall be carried out within one year from the date of approval. 3.1.2 verifies implementation per the approval documentation and suitability to the plant, that the PMS produces the Annual Audit documentation, and that onboard personnel are familiar with it. 3.1.3 on satisfactory survey a report is submitted and the approved PMS may replace the CMS.

3.2.1: the annual audit is carried out by a Society's surveyor and PREFERABLY concurrently with the annual survey of machinery. 3.2.2 the surveyor reviews the annual report or verifies that the Society has reviewed it.
A footnote records that the term 'audit' in this context is NOT related to ISM audit.

sources.title: Loss of the Panama-flagged bulk carrier OCEAN WINNER (IMO 9145530) in the Bay of Bengal, 21 August 2026 - the evidence set supporting QB2_A#q31
sources.edition: Evidence as at 5 September 2026
sources.issuing_authority: MULTIPLE - and none of them is a casualty investigating authority
sources.issuing_authority_note: THE POINT OF THIS ROW IS WHAT IT CANNOT OFFER. Panama is the flag State and therefore the marine safety investigating State under the Casualty Investigation Code ch. 6.2; it has published NO report. India has published no report. No owner or manager statement was located. The source tiers available are therefore (2) an official authority quoted in reporting, (4) contemporaneous news, and a commercial ship register for vessel particulars. Tier 1 does not exist yet.
sources.source_type: official statements quoted in contemporaneous reporting, plus ship registers
sources.authority_rank: SECONDARY throughout for the casualty facts. The regulatory content of QB2_A#q31 does NOT rest on this row - it rests on the IMSBC Code and res. MSC.255(84).
sources.access_note: No bytes are held because no casualty document exists to hold. This is not an access restriction that was worked around; it is the absence of a published investigation, and the card says so to the candidate.
sources.checked_how: Every candidate-facing fact in QB2_A#q31 was verified INDIVIDUALLY against at least two independent reports rather than the card being checked as a whole. Three facts failed and were corrected; two more were removed as unverifiable. See verified_claims and claims_NOT_established.
sources.revalidation_note: A Panamanian or Indian safety investigation report supersedes the whole factual half of QB2_A#q31 and none of its regulatory half. Until one exists the card must keep saying the cause is undetermined.
verified_claims: Vessel: OCEAN WINNER, IMO 9145530, Panama flag, bulk carrier built 1998. Corroborated across The Maritime Executive, Global Times and independent commercial registers.
About 225 m length overall and about 72,900 tonnes deadweight (commercial registers); reported in the press rounded as '70,000 dwt'. Panamax.
Loaded iron ore fines at Paradip, Odisha and sailed 20 August 2026.
Sank 21 August 2026 at about 1645 GMT; the AIS signal ceased at the same time as the distress alert (The Maritime Executive; Global Times, 'Friday at approximately 4:45 pm GMT').
24 crew: 20 Chinese, 3 Myanmar nationals, 1 Bangladeshi. 2 Chinese crew found on a liferaft; 22 missing.
The two survivors, named in reporting as Pan Tonglai and Chen Jianhe, were landed at Paradip by Indian Coast Guard Ship VARAD on 22 August 2026.

The heavy list and the 'about eight minutes' to sink are the SURVIVORS' account, relayed publicly by Shyam Jagannathan, India's Director General of Shipping / Maritime Administration. The card attributes it that way and does not state it as an established mechanism.
Search coordinated by the Indian Coast Guard with Indian Navy assets, jointly with MRCC Beijing.
No cause has been determined and no investigation report has been published.
claims_NOT_established: THE CARGO TONNAGE IS REPORTED, NOT CERTIFICATED. Reporting gives 71,200 tonnes. The card previously said 72,100 tonnes, which no source supports and which is a transposition; it now says 71,200 and labels it as reported.

THE DISTANCE OFFSHORE IS DISPUTED, AND THE CARD'S OLD HEDGE WAS ON THE WRONG SIDE OF IT. Reports give about 230 nautical miles (Global Times) and about 290 nautical miles (PTI via Outlook India). The card previously said '230 to 240', a range whose upper limb no source supports while a materially higher figure was in circulation. The card now gives 230 to 290 and tells the candidate not to commit to one figure. The legal conclusion is unaffected: every reported distance is beyond the 200-mile EEZ.
THE BEAM IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The card previously said '32.26 m'. Registers give '32 m'. The false precision has been removed and no beam is now claimed.

THE RESCUING VESSEL IS NOT AS THE CARD SAID. It previously said the survivors were 'recovered from liferafts by a passing tanker'. No source supports a passing tanker; the verified facts are a liferaft and ICGS VARAD landing them at Paradip.
THE DESTINATION IS DISPUTED - Singapore in some reports, China in others. The card asserts neither.
THE CAUSE. Liquefaction is the leading industry hypothesis and the card says exactly that. No cargo moisture content, no TML value and no certificate content is known.
The owner, manager, class society and P&I club were not established and are not named.
